newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Carnarvon Basin tops crude output.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Carnarvon Basin tops crude output.

text.p: Australia's total crude oil and condensate output jumped to 595,200 barrels per day (bpd) in December, the highest level since March 1990, from 533,600 bpd in November, the Department of Primary Industries and Energy reported on Monday.
This jump reflected the highest monthly oil and gas output yet from the Carnarvon Basin offshore Western Australia, the department said in its Australian Petroleum Statistics monthly.
Carnarvon Basin production amounted to 355,300 bpd, nearly double the 189,600 bpd produced in the offshore Gippsland Basin.
Department figures show that the Carnarvon Basin overtook the Gippsland Basin's Bass Strait fields as Australia's largest oil producing province in calendar 1996.
Carnarvon Basin output rose to 285,000 bpd in 1996 from 215,300 in 1995 while Gippsland Basin production fell to 198,900 bpd from 215,300 bpd.

It said the increase in Carnarvon Basin production from around 80,000 bpd in January 1994 came over the last three years as several projects, including Wanaea/Cossack, Griffin, East Spar and Goodwyn have come into production.
"The Carnarvon Basin in now established as Australia's major oil producing region," the department said.
National crude and condensate production rose to 544,200 bpd in calendar 1996 from 510,900 bpd in 1995.

The department said that if December's output was maintained for the next few years, Australia's petroleum self-sufficiency would rise to around 78 percent from about 70 percent in fiscal 1995/96 ended June 30.
Its figures show 1995/96 crude output was 521,800 bpd, down from 537,500 bpd in 1994/95.
